# Managed Service for Apache Airflow version list 




















This page describes the released versions of Managed Airflow images.

## About Managed Service for Apache Airflow images

Managed Service for Apache Airflow images bundle Airflow releases with other common binaries
and Python libraries. These Docker images are versioned in the following way:

- 

In Managed Airflow (Gen 3), new Airflow builds become available with
each Managed Airflow release. When you create an environment, as
an option, you can specify a specific build to use with the chosen Airflow
version. After an environment is created, it keeps using the same build of
Airflow until you upgrade it to a later build or a later version of Airflow.

- 

In Managed Airflow (Gen 2) and Managed Airflow (Legacy Gen 1), new images become available with
each Managed Airflow release. When you create an environment, you
specify an image version to use. After an environment is created, it keeps
using the specified image version until you upgrade it to a later version.

## Default and latest versions in Managed Airflow (Gen 3)

Latest versions in Managed Airflow (Gen 3) are most recently released builds of
Airflow. If a release contains two Airflow versions, both of them are marked as
the latest version in the [list of images](#images).

In Managed Airflow (Gen 3), the default version is one of the latest versions. When
you create a Managed Airflow (Gen 3) environment without specifying an Airflow
version, this version and build of Airflow are used.

## Default and latest versions in Managed Airflow (Gen 2)

Latest versions in Managed Airflow (Gen 2) are most recently released Managed Airflow images. Each Managed Airflow version supports more than one
Airflow version.

In Managed Airflow (Gen 2), the default version is one of the latest versions. If you
don't specify an image version when you create a Managed Airflow (Gen 2)
environment, the image that is marked as the default version is used.

## Versions with an extended upgrade timeline

We label some Managed Airflow versions and Airflow builds as extended
upgrade timeline versions. Extended upgrade timeline versions have the
following differences compared to regular versions:

- You can upgrade your environment to this version for 18 months after the
release date.

- You can create an environment with this version for 18 months after the
release date.

## Maintenance release versions of Managed Airflow (Legacy Gen 1)

Maintenance release versions of Managed Airflow (Legacy Gen 1) are new Managed Airflow (Legacy Gen 1)
images that provide only bug fixes and small improvements.

Support dates for maintenance release versions correspond to the support dates
of the last Managed Airflow (Legacy Gen 1) version 1.20.12 that
was released on April 25, 2023.

## Versions with disabled upgrades

For some versions of Managed Airflow images, it is not possible to
upgrade an environment to a later version:

- composer-1.7.7-airflow-1.10.2

- composer-1.7.7-airflow-1.10.1

- composer-1.7.7-airflow-1.9.0

If you use a version with disabled upgrades, we recommend to create a new
environment side-by-side, then migrate all your DAGs to the new environment.
Once you confirm that the new environment works, delete the environment with
disabled upgrades if you don't need it anymore.

## Version support dates

Each Managed Airflow (Gen 2) image and Managed Airflow (Gen 3) Airflow build has a release date and one or more support dates associated with it:

- 

The support dates are based on Managed Airflow
[version deprecation and support periods](/composer/docs/composer-versioning-overview#version-deprecation-and-support).

- 

You might see discrepancies in support end dates between this documentation
and Google Cloud Dedicated console UI. For clarity, consider the later of these dates
as the official end of support.

The image releases aren't simultaneous across Google Cloud Dedicated in Germany regions. This
means the Google Cloud Dedicated console indicates a support end date that is one year
after the image was released in your specific region, based on
Managed Airflow
[version deprecation and support periods](/composer/docs/composer-versioning-overview#version-deprecation-and-support).

For Managed Airflow versions with an
[extended upgrade timeline](#extended-upgrade-timeline), this duration might
occasionally be longer than one year. However, this documentation refers to
the initial release date in the first region.

## End of life dates

Managed Airflow (Legacy Gen 1) and Managed Airflow (Gen 2) environments with version 2.0.x are
approaching their end of life.

On the end of life date listed for these versions, the environments with these
versions **will stop working** and you will no longer be able to use them.

## Available upgrade choices in Managed Airflow (Gen 2)

- 

In Google Cloud Dedicated console, you can create a new environment or
[upgrade](/composer/docs/composer-2/upgrade-environments) an existing environment only using one of the
[latest supported versions](#composer-2-latest-default) of
Managed Airflow (Gen 2).

- 

In Google Cloud CLI, API, or Terraform, you can create a new environment
using any version that is still within its full support date.

- 

In Google Cloud CLI, API, or Terraform, you can upgrade an existing
environment to the latest supported versions, three previous
versions of Managed Airflow (Gen 2), the last patch version of the
previous minor version, and to versions with an extended upgrade timeline.
It's not possible to upgrade to other versions of
Managed Airflow (Gen 2), even if they are still supported and can be used
to create a new environment.

Example of upgrade choices for Google Cloud CLI, API, and Terraform:

- Latest versions: `composer-2.11.5-airflow-*`

- Three previous Managed Airflow (Gen 2) versions:
`composer-2.11.4-airflow-*`, `composer-2.11.3-airflow-*`,
`composer-2.11.2-airflow-*`.

- Last patch of the previous Managed Airflow (Gen 2) minor version:
`composer-2.10.2-airflow-*`

- Managed Airflow (Gen 2) versions with an extended upgrade timeline:
`composer-2.10.2-airflow-*`, `composer-2.10.1-ariflow-*`,
`composer-2.9.7-airflow-*`, and other versions with an extended upgrade
timeline.
